description:
FILED + FIXED s440 (Fable), FOUND BY THE SHAPES CORPUS (Pl/t/shapes/punct-arrays-glob.pl: snippet S05's `glob("~")` came after S04's `<~>` and answered 0).

WHAT IT WAS: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp p-glob--list-context kept a per-pattern :list-done mark ("first call returns all matches; second call with same pattern returns empty" -- its own docstring, from f92d2a4 2026-04-11, the defins.t scalar-iterator commit), so every SECOND list-context glob of a pattern -- anywhere in the program -- returned nothing, and because the list call also remhash'ed the scalar iterator, `while (my $f = glob(P)) { my @i = glob(P) }` never terminated.  PRE-EXISTING (identical on 4a7c5a0, before s438i/#450); never seen because no gate row and no sweep file repeats a list glob of one pattern.

    for (1..3) { my @f = glob("gd/*.c"); print scalar(@f) }      perl 2 2 2    PCL 2 0 2
    sub n { my @f = glob("gd/*.c"); scalar @f } print n(), n()   perl 22       PCL 20
    my @a = <gd/*.c>; my @b = <gd/*.c>;                          perl 2 2      PCL 2 0
    while (my $f = glob(P)) { $c++; my @i = glob(P) }            perl 22 c=2   PCL infinite

FIX: list context expands and returns EVERY match, every call, and touches no iterator state (perl keys its scalar iterator by CALL SITE, PCL by pattern -- #489 -- so a list glob must not disturb a scalar loop elsewhere); :list-done is gone.  The scalar-context iterator (`while (my $f = glob(P))`, `while (($x) = glob(P))` under *p-in-list-assign-rhs*) is unchanged.  Guard: Pl/t/glob-01.t (two oracle rows, perl-probed, inverse-run on a 4a7c5a0 worktree: `2 0 2` and the infinite loop).  Runtime-only -> the full sweep runs with the s441 batch (Fable).

NOTE left open (pre-existing, deliberate, documented in p-glob's docstring): `while (($x) = glob(P))` iterates one file per pass in PCL (the readline mirror) where perl's list assignment makes it loop forever -- no valid perl program has that shape, so it stays.
subject: DONE s440: a LIST-context glob returned the full list, then EMPTY, then full ... per pattern (`for (1..3) { my @f = glob("*.c") }` gave 2 0 2; a sub calling glob twice answered nothing the second time; a scalar glob loop with a list glob of the same pattern inside it was INFINITE) -- perl: list context is never stateful
